restrictions: Messages of 55 and 63 bytes (the 63-byte one ends in eight zero bytes): one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and the true block length; unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision of two distinct complete messages.

Cancellation, constants, class of Y4, rule A, Lemma N: c66f230d (Jbenisek, co-author tekkac). Three-level construction, per-outer-step table, staged batch with halting budgets: 60f94c5c (Jbenisek). Run-average premise tested by a preregistered uniform sample with Lemma C' and the empirical Bernstein rule, and a 2^39-trial sample of the 098e66f4 configuration: 52bb50ee (Subflatus3); sampling single uniform batches (Lemma U): 1d5e54ce (Subflatus3). Budgets 1/6000 above the premises: 5266c5ce (leech1996). Member values once per outer step: df8bd46d (Th0rgal); lanes: ticket 2bf40fb (tekkac); complement propagation: 8c81a219 (Th0rgal). Jbenisek, tekkac, Th0rgal, Subflatus3 and leech1996 are co-authors.

Ours (18a7fc52, d26a3c5f, 2bb5d604, 098e66f4, 21252124): S8, beta filter (Lemma B), Lemmas D and D', exact S8 count, block accumulator, stage C, a random word per outer step, exact stage values, Chernoff bound on the budgets, D3.d1 = X3 (X14 = 0); new: the loop order S2K (X2 table, batches of seven X2 values of one member, Lemma A3), pass-flag tests (Lemmas A3, F2), one-operation budget counts with a halt test per group, and a preregistered per-batch sample of this order. Not used: the sub-class, eight-condition rule, E1 test stage and budget premises of 60f94c5c.

Exact part: for every eight 32-bit words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7 (Theorem 1), with Y4 in S8; the batches of the order S2K (per outer step, member, group g < 9,363 and position i < 2^16, lane l holding the trial with C2.a1 = (7g + l) 2^16 + i) cover every trial exactly once (the last group's lanes 2..6 repeat group 0 and are masked); stage A passes a lane iff its trial satisfies rule A (Lemma A3, also checked exhaustively on 2^28 cases), stage B iff it satisfies rule A and the beta filter (Lemma F2), and stage C computes the XOR differences of digest words 1, 3, 4 and 6 exactly (Lemmas D, D'). Every good trial (R = 0, rule A, filter) reaches stage C and is found unless a budget has halted the run.

Given H1 (ii), a budget halt (more than E - 2^16 entries) has probability below exp(-6.9 * 10^6) for stage B and exp(-2.0 * 10^5) for stage C (Theorem 2: Chernoff bound over the independent outer steps, for stage C after a union bound inside a batch; no independence inside an outer step, member, group or batch is used). Heuristic part: N = 1,512,538 * 2^80 = 2^100.53 trials.

256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers (peak 62); seven trials per word in 36-bit lanes; stage A 19 operations for every batch, stage B 66 for at most E_B = ceil(0.5766 * 6001/6000 * p_B * V * 2^64 * 9,363) = 2^94.5999 batches (p_B = 0.1992628), stage C 119 for at most E_C = ceil(1.002 * 6001/6000 * N * 2^-11) = 2^89.5317 batches (count-down budget registers, 1 operation per entry, a halt test before each group of 2^16 batches; stages B and C duplicated for each unrolled position); with the block update (4 per 256 batches), group set-up, block test and end (25 per group), member step (112), X2 table (94 per word, 2^32 + 2^16 words per outer step) and outer step with its random word (274): 3.8600 operations per trial, every executed primitive including loads, stores and random words counted as 1; no sorting or lookup by value.

The time bound holds for every value of the coins. Total 2^93.735734, claimed 93.7358 (holds up to 3.86018 operations per trial; budget registers in memory 2^93.7483, a loop over positions 2^93.8870).

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step (V * 2^32 words; three 32-bit words of each are used, vc, S15 and S9; D3.d1 = X3 is fixed). Success probability 0.39 holds only under H1, the only heuristic, with parts (i) and (ii). The factor F = 92,675,072 = 2^26.4657 in H1 (i) is assumed; it is half of an exact model count of 185,350,144 (margin 2.000), recomputed by the shipped program's --count mode, that the organizer experiments do not measure. H1 (ii) asserts, as run averages over the batches of the order S2K and over the trials, 0.5766 times the exact model value p_B of the event that a batch enters stage B and 1.002 times the exact model rate 2^-11 of rule A with the filter; both values were set by a preregistered decision rule from a uniform sample of 2^38 trials of this order (measured 0.57650 and 0.99987), with budgets 6001/6000 times them. With the uniform rate the same search gives about 120.2. No full collision is exhibited.

Preprocessing: a declared upper-bound charge (not a premise; H1 and the success bound do not use it) of 2^86 units (2^94.75 word operations) covers all selection of the stored constants, class, rule A, sub-class, filter, stage tests and block constants, of the order of the construction, the staged batch and the loop order S2K, and of the premise and budget conventions, by c66f230d, 60f94c5c, 52bb50ee, 5266c5ce, 1d5e54ce and by us, without reliance on run records (more than 2^34 times c66f230d's own estimate). Memory 2^100 bytes bounds that preprocessing by its charged work; the search itself uses under 2^42 bytes (the X2 table of an outer step under 2^41). Advice under 64 bytes.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's random words (one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step, supplying vc, S15 and S9; D3.d1 = X3), (i) the N = 1,512,538 * 2^80 trials of proof.md Section 4 behave, with respect to the event good (128-bit residual R = 0, rule A, and E1's c1 passes the beta filter), like independent events of probability at least F * 2^-128 each (F = 92,675,072 = 185,350,144 / 2 = 2^26.4657), to the extent that the probability that no trial is good is at most exp(-lambda) + 0.002 with lambda = N * F * 2^-128 = 0.4980001; and (ii) averaged over the V * 2^64 * 9,363 batches of the run in the order S2K of proof.md Section 4, the probability that a batch has a trial taking part in its decisions that satisfies rule A is at most 0.5766 * p_B, and averaged over the N trials, the probability that a trial satisfies rule A and passes the beta filter is at most 1.002 * 2^-11, where p_B = 32,052,445,611,625 / 160,855,115,169,792 = 0.1992628 and 2^-11 are the exact values of these two stage events under the seven-word model M that gives the count of (i), with the distinct trials of a batch independent as in (i). The values 0.5766 and 1.002 were set by the preregistered decision rule of proof.md Section 8.2 (52bb50ee's empirical Bernstein and Lemma C' tests on a grid) from a uniform sample of single batches of this order whose runs, seeds and analysis were fixed by the preregistration; no other sample or run was used to set them; the stage-B value lies below the M value because rule A clusters, and rests on that sample, not on M.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 4: lengths 55 and 63, the six constants of Fact P, the construction of Section 2, Y4 in the sub-class S8 of Section 3, the three words vc, S15, S9 from the outer step's own random word and D3.d1 = X3 (so X14 = 0), vd below 1,512,538, w5 and X2 over 2^32 values each, all 65,536 members; batched in the order S2K (per outer step, member, group g < 9,363 and position i < 2^16, lane l the trial with C2.a1 = (7g + l) 2^16 + i; the last group's lanes 2..6 masked); rule A as in Lemma A; the filter (c1 AND 00098188) = 00008000. Part (ii) concerns averages over all batches and all trials of the run, not single contexts, members, groups or batches.
heuristics.extrapolation: (i) From an exact count under the seven-word model M (proof.md Section 8.1): restricted to the six betas of T6, which the filter contains by Lemma B, the share of solutions of R = 0 with rule A among Y4 in S8 times 2^192 is 185,350,144 * 2^-128, an exact integer from 57 nonzero of 85 outcomes counted by carry automata in exact integer arithmetic without sampling (equal with and without rule A). The shipped program recomputes it: python3 experiments/s8stage.py --count (about 2 minutes). Our C counter, the Python port and a separately written counter agree exactly; a sampling estimator gives ratio 1.0007 +- 0.0047; every member of S8 has an exact factor of at least 184.57M; the full-class parts equal the published table of c66f230d; brute force at 8-bit words agrees. On real trials, rule-A and filter rates agree with the model at rates 2^-5 to 2^-11, the E1 part has real/model 1.0086 over 2^33.8 trials, E3 partial events of probability about 2^-38 show the counter's S8-versus-rest ratios on real trials as on model draws, and with D3.d1 = X3 the E1 events and the 2^-14 E3 event keep the rates of random D3.d1 (ratios 0.9996 to 1.0002), while the 2^-30 event on the low halves of D1 and D3 has ratio 0.82 +- 0.13 (0.87 +- 0.09 against all random-D3.d1 counts), consistent with equality (2^38 against 2^36 trials). F is exactly half of the count. (ii) Under M, h1 and c1 are independent uniform words; rule A holds for 2^27 of 2^32 words h1 and the filter for 2^26 of 2^32 words c1, so rule A with the filter has rate exactly 2^-11, and a batch of seven (last group: two) distinct independent trials has a rule-A trial with probability 1 - (31/32)^7 (1 - (31/32)^2), giving p_B. The values of (ii) are not extrapolated from M: they are run averages estimated by uniform sampling of the run's own index space. A preregistered uniform sample of this order (proof.md Section 8.2; 2^38 trials in 39,271,268,352 i.i.d. units, each one batch of the run drawn uniformly: outer step with vd, w5, vc, S15, S9 uniform, D3.d1 = X3, a uniform member, group and position; its unit counts equal the forward computation of the counted program 3aef733e (the shipped program before its PREMISE line was set; they differ only in that line) on 35,000 drawn units, 3,000 of them also through its counted pieces) gives a stage-B share of 0.57650 +- 0.00001 of p_B (empirical Bernstein bound 0.57658 p_B at delta = 2^-64; Lemma C' exponent 66.8 at the premise) and a rule-A-and-filter rate of 0.99987 +- 0.00009 of 2^-11 (empirical Bernstein 1.00070; Lemma C' exponent 43.6 at the premise); per run of 2^33 trials 0.5764 to 0.5766 p_B and 0.9986 to 1.0006 * 2^-11. The extrapolation is from this sample to the averages over all 2^100.53 trials and 2^97.7 batches of the run.
heuristics.limitations: The factor of (i) is assumed, set at exactly half of a model count that organizer experiments do not measure (margin 2.000). M is untested at probability 2^-100.5; real trials were compared with it for events down to about 2^-38 per trial (E1 part, E3 partial events, random D3.d1) and 2^-30 (with D3.d1 = X3) and about 2^-40 for one call in c66f230d; the full E3 event has too few hits at our sample size to test. M fails inside one context for rule A (clustering); only averages are measured, and part (ii) and Theorem 2 use only such averages. The constants, class and rule A were chosen by c66f230d to maximize a count of this kind; S8 is the best under M of 8,992,320 sub-classes and supplies a factor 1.29 of the margin (the full class with rule A counts 1.555 F >= F); the filter was chosen to contain the heaviest betas; choices that are best under M may favour parameters where M overstates. 37% of the S8 count comes from one beta, 18b0e098. Trials of one outer step share its three coin words (D3.d1 = X3 in all outer steps) and trials of one context differ only in Y4; for (i) their independence is assumed. With D3.d1 = X3, X14 = 0 in every trial, so C2 runs with d = 0 and C2.d1 = ROR(a1, 16) (its outputs Y6, an E1 input, and Y14, an E3 input, still vary with X2, X6 and X10, but no longer with a coin in the d input), and X9 = S9 + X3 varies only with the coin S9; the E1 events, the 2^-14 E3 event and the 2^-30 event were measured again in this configuration (the first two equal to random D3.d1 within 0.05%, the 2^-30 event at 0.82 +- 0.13 of it, 1.4 standard errors below 1), the E1-part ratio and the per-outcome 2^-38 E3 partial events were not; H1 (i) assumes they keep their rates. Part (ii) is estimated from a uniform sample of 2^38 trials of this order, not from the 2^100.5 of the run, and only on the participant side with a seeded generator; the stage-B premise exceeds the observed mean only by a factor 1.00017: it is the smallest grid value above the sample's 2^-64 empirical Bernstein bound 0.57658 (standard error 0.00001), so it rests on the sample's size and on the correctness of the sampler (cross-checked unit by unit against the counted program 3aef733e, which differs from the shipped program only in the PREMISE line, on 35,000 units, 3,000 of them through its counted pieces), not on a reserve. One organizer run of 256 clustered seeds has a stage-B ratio with expectation about 0.5765 and standard deviation about 0.067, so about half of all runs exceed the premise; one run is not evidence for or against this run average. D3.d1 = X3 changes how rule A clusters in a batch: stage-B share 0.5765 p_B against 0.6320 p_B with random D3.d1 in the same sample, at equal per-trial rule-A rate; (ii) measures this in the algorithm's configuration, and H1 (i) assumes it does not extend to the event good. The order S2K was chosen after an exploratory pilot of four batchings (disclosed with its results in proof.md Section 8.2); the premises rest only on the preregistered sample. The stage-B share depends on the order (21252124's order: 0.539 p_B). The organizer experiments see the stage events in 16,128 clustered lanes per run. The count program runs on the participant side (about 2 minutes), not as an organizer experiment. Run selection: no organizer-run count or frequency supports F or the averages of (ii); the experiments' predictions are exact per-seed predicates; every recorded replay of the shipped program is reported (proof.md Section 6: 41 participant-run local replays with program, harness and nonces hashed before running, all exact); every run of the preregistered sample, its development runs and the pilot are reported (proof.md Section 8.2, Run selection); no parameter, version, seed or nonce was chosen on replay or sample outcomes, and the only change after the sample is the PREMISE line set by the preregistered rule.
